criteria.reason: Deterministic inputs and executable pair/count checks are supported by the preserved Oracle/alternative results. Verifier tooling is baked; hundreds of repetitions have not been run.
The accepted Oracle and independent alternative each passed all 333 cases with reward 1 within the configured resources. The expert implementation time remains an estimate.
Numerical compatibility and weighted counting are real engineering concerns, but professional difficulty at the TB3 bar has not been established by independent expert review or model evidence.
Reducing cohort-scale survival-model evaluation cost while preserving its public metric behavior is a realistic ML maintenance task.
Tests call public APIs and compare outputs, errors, warnings and process duration. No specific algorithm or source layout is graded.
Agent image excludes tests/Oracle; the separate verifier uses root-protected expected answers and unprivileged subprocesses. No adversarial trials or blanket security guarantee are claimed.

Reviewed task code performs ordinary package setup, numerical work and bounded subprocess verification; it does not read credentials, mount host sockets or transmit task data. This is source review, not an exploit test.
Submitted code is executed through public APIs; numerical grading does not scan candidate source keywords.

Digest-pinned base, pinned Python packages, seeded workloads and offline verification support reproducibility. APT is intentionally unpinned; timing variation is handled by the existing two-attempt policy.
The intended work is numerical/algorithmic compatibility and scaling; there is no bespoke output-format puzzle or artificially prescribed algorithm.
The audit maps APIs/defaults/keywords, pairs, weights, errors, warnings, numerics, timing and artifacts to actual tests or harness enforcement. Selected coverage is not exhaustive API proof.
No new originality claim is made. Whether this concrete integration problem is sufficiently distinct from known concordance optimizations still needs reviewer judgment.
Source inspection, implementation and profiling provide a multi-step workflow, but one-shot solvability has not been measured; no model trial has run.
The instruction gives statistical rules; readable pair/Fraction, blocked and analytical references derive expected results independently of the optimized implementation.
Absolute paths, outcome-based requirements and no algorithm hints are satisfied, but the instruction is explicitly AI-generated. The upstream human-written instruction requirement is unresolved.

The 691-word agent-facing contract, excluding canary/trailer, describes actual compatibility, artifact and timing requirements. It contains no unrelated instruction-bearing resources or repeated procedure.
solve.sh applies a source patch implementing actual computation and runs a public-API smoke check. Expected final scores are not hardcoded as the solution.
Only /app/work is transferred; tests and tools are baked. Shared runtime lock and licenses byte-match; no undeclared agent state is required.
Agent context contains baseline source/runtime/license only. Verifier dependencies are baked, and both Dockerfiles update/clean APT appropriately.
Both API call signatures, defaults, five ordered numeric results, count types, exceptions and numerical comparison policy are stated.
API and runtime paths were checked against the source and current static scripts; no identifier typo was found.
Three sentences identify compatibility reasoning, synthetic data and the real-world ML engineering role. No model scores are used to assert intrinsic difficulty.
The time sweep/Fenwick strategy, equal-time handling, separate weighting and compatibility paths match the actual reference patch.
The paragraph identifies numerical/reference checks, calibration rationale and two correct implementations, and states the accepted 333-case outcomes accurately.
ML / Evaluation and the survival-analysis, concordance, numerical-correctness, performance and Python tags describe the actual task.
survival-concordance is a descriptive two-token lowercase slug and matches its package name.
One CPU / 2 GiB and the preserved 1200-second verifier budget cover the measured correct runs and 609.324-second Nop suite. The 14400-second agent budget is unchanged.

All four explanations and matching configuration metadata are present, with concise license/build context. AI provenance and missing identity fields are disclosed; authorship compliance is not claimed.
The configured three-hour estimate is nonzero and plausible as an estimate, but it has not been independently confirmed by a timed expert implementation.
The exact pinned Harbor Task parser accepted the configuration. The rubric inventory omits the supported network_mode field; that upstream inventory drift is not a reason to modify the valid task.
The 26-file package contains required scaffold, code, verifier tools, pins and licenses. Backups, references, worksheets, logs and development tooling remain outside it.
The small editable module and optional helpers live under /app/work; cache, bytecode, git and virtualenv directories are excluded. No large fixed dataset or dependency tree is transferred.

The unchanged harness drops to UID/GID 10001 with no supplementary groups and no new privileges, protects reward paths, captures temporary-file output and kills the process group; preserved reports verify 60 child identities.
All three preserved reports contain 333 unique case IDs with matching summaries, no skipped/pending/other outcomes and raw/final outcome consistency.

The instruction preserves public behavior through executable checks rather than protecting source bytes. Installed reference state is isolated and hash-checked; no cosmetic protected-file rule is introduced.
Scoreable pytest success/failure paths write exactly 1 or 0. Infrastructure failures abort without a scoreable reward; no fractional reward is written.
